mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, which compresses wage growth and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary environment, which increases both discount rates and cost pressures, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for three consecutive months during a period when the unemployment rate is below 5% signals labor market overheating, which precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated Fed tightening.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a residential investment recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a broad-based strengthening of consumer demand, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-mo MA AND RSAFS > 12-mo MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.
